summary: Hunted an intermittent header/inspector mismatch in the Gizmo web client by attaching a Playwright watcher to the user's live Chrome session over CDP. Caught two real cases: a startup window where the header sat on the previously-selected workspace until a 2,678-message thread finished resuming, and a stale-write race where the workspace context landed on whichever async response returned last regardless of which thread was actually open.
decisions: Bug is a stale-write race in workspace selection: selectWorkspace and switchSession both write selectedProjectPath and then await, with no generation counter, so a slower earlier response can reassert a workspace after the user has navigated away.

Two prior fixes already applied and typechecked but not deployed: refreshProjects() no longer reassigns workspace to projects[0] without checking the open session; rebindSelection() now re-derives workspace from the open session on reconnect.
Fix for the race will mirror the existing #selectionVersion counter used for thread switches, extending the same guard to workspace switches.
Watcher's switch-watch.log is the source of truth for confirming the fix against the live window before deploying.
errors: Startup reproduce script /tmp/startup.mjs was interrupted by the user before completing.

Two prior background watcher processes (bmockiq41, bsalyc4p9) were marked stopped when the previous Claude session ended without a completion marker; the surviving switch-watch.log still shows the mismatches they were meant to catch live.
